name: Fruit juices, non-apple
anchor: Per-form sovereign beverage cells in the as-consumed liquid basis (EU 2023/915 juice and rice-drink cells, Codex CXS 193 fruit juices, EU 2024/1987 beverage nickel, EU canned-beverage tin, Hong Kong Cap 132V's named carbonated, tea, coffee and wine beverage entries, and the US and Hong Kong packaged-drinking-water quality standards), with dry leaf, bean and powder commodities anchored separately in their own as-sold basis and never converted between the two
native_basis_label: ready-to-drink liquid, as consumed (wet weight, single strength); a concentrate or a powder-to-liquid product is assessed as reconstituted to single strength per the manufacturer's own directions, which is the basis EU 2023/915 and Codex CXS 193 write into their juice cells and Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 writes into its beverage entries
scope_note: Single-strength ready-to-drink fruit juices, fruit juices from concentrate, concentrated fruit juices assessed as reconstituted, and fruit nectars, in every packaging format (carton, PET, glass, can, pouch), containing no apple juice or apple-derived juice solids. Any apple content routes the product to the apple-containing row, which carries the stricter inorganic-arsenic ceiling. Grape and berry juices sit in this row and are held to the strictest applicable cell rather than to their own looser government-written splits, which are disclosed. Rice-based and other plant-based drinks are not juices and route to the plant-milk rows; drinking water and mineral water route to Category 8; a juice carrying a Supplement Facts panel routes to Category 16; an infant or young-child juice-based drink routes to Category 1.
basis_guard: as[ _]consumed|wet weight|reconstituted|ready.to.drink|product as placed on market|\bjuice\b|single-strength|bottled water|portion ordinarily consumed
basis_guard_note: This row publishes a ready-to-drink liquid ceiling, so every named anchor must itself be written in a wet as-consumed (or as-placed-on-market liquid, or packaged-drinking-water) basis. The guard refuses any dry-commodity as-sold cell, any feed-basis cell, any food-contact migration limit and any article-content limit, because applying a dry leaf, bean or powder maximum level to a brewed or reconstituted liquid would be exactly the basis conflation Method v2.0 forbids. No brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented in either direction.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact beverage form and analyte in the row's declared native basis, with disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination where a species is bounded or is a method artifact, and a control where no defensible sovereign number and no supportable near-neighbour exist. Never occurrence-derived. Ready-to-drink and dry-commodity bases are never mixed and no brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented.

Pb.basis: wet weight, single-strength ready-to-drink juice; a concentrate is assessed as reconstituted to the original juice concentration, which is the basis the instruments themselves write
Pb.label: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.1.19.2 sets lead in fruit juices, fruit juices from concentrate, concentrated fruit juices and fruit nectars other than those exclusively from berries and other small fruits at 30 ug/kg; Codex CXS 193 sets fruit juices at 30 ug/kg and Hong Kong Cap 132V sets the same commodity at 30 ug/kg. Three credible sovereigns converge on 30 ug/kg and the EU cell binds on jurisdiction priority.
Pb.substantiation: This is a direct regulatory lookup, not a calculation. The candidate set deliberately includes the looser government-written splits so the selection is auditable: grape juice at 40 ug/kg (Codex and Hong Kong) and juices exclusively from berries and other small fruits at 50 ug/kg (EU 2023/915 section 3.1.19.1 and Hong Kong), plus the older US FDA Juice HACCP hazard-control level of 50 ug/kg. Because the whole non-apple fruit-juice family is certified as a single row, the row ceiling is the strictest applicable value across every form in scope, 30 ug/kg. That is deliberate over-compliance for grape and berry juices relative to their own government-written cells, and it is disclosed here rather than buried: a grape or berry juice that meets 40 or 50 ug/kg is lawful in the EU, Codex and Hong Kong but is not HMTc-certifiable in this row. The US FDA 2022 draft action levels for lead in juice (10 ug/kg for single-strength apple juice, 20 ug/kg for other single-strength juices and blends) are DRAFT guidance expressly not for implementation and are therefore not eligible anchors; they are recorded so that the register's gated draft rows are visibly accounted for rather than silently omitted.

Cd.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a cadmium maximum level for a fruit juice. EU 2023/915's cadmium cells cover vegetables, cereals, oilseeds, pulses, cocoa and chocolate, meat, fish and mushrooms; Codex CXS 193, FSANZ Schedule 19, Health Canada and Hong Kong Cap 132V likewise set no cadmium maximum level for fruit or for fruit juice. The nearest sovereign cadmium cells are written for vegetable commodities in a fresh-weight basis and for a different botanical family, so they are not applicable to a fruit juice. No near-neighbour read-across is supportable, so the fail-safe disposition is a control: cadmium testing is mandatory on every certified lot and no ceiling is invented from occurrence data.
Cd.reference_method: Cadmium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result above 10 ug/kg in a ready-to-drink form, or above 100 ug/kg in a dry form, escalates to an ingredient-origin and process-water investigation and is a Standards Ratchet surveillance input under Governance Policy section 12.

tAs.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-arsenic maximum level for a fruit juice. Regulators write beverage arsenic limits on the inorganic species (EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit juices at 20 ug/kg and section 3.4.1.6 non-alcoholic rice-based drinks at 30 ug/kg; the US FDA apple-juice action level at 10 ug/kg) and write unspeciated arsenic limits only in the packaged-water and public-water-supply schedules, which are Category 8 instruments. The inorganic-arsenic ceiling in this row carries the health-relevant fraction. Total arsenic is therefore mandatory on every lot as the parent screen and no total-arsenic ceiling is invented.
tAs.reference_method: Total arsenic by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) is reflexed whenever total arsenic exceeds 50 percent of this row's inorganic-arsenic ceiling, or 20 ug/kg where this row publishes no inorganic-arsenic number. Species never substitute for the total: the iAs result does not satisfy the tAs reporting requirement.

iAs.basis: wet weight, single-strength ready-to-drink juice (or concentrate as reconstituted)
iAs.label: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.4.4 sets inorganic arsenic in fruit juices, concentrated fruit juices as reconstituted, and fruit nectars at 20 ug/kg, which is the strictest applicable value and binds; Health Canada's grape juice and grape nectar cell (30 ug/kg) is the looser sibling and is disclosed.
iAs.substantiation: Direct sovereign maximum level for this exact product form and basis. The US FDA inorganic-arsenic action level of 10 ug/kg is final guidance but is scoped to apple juice specifically and is not applicable to a non-apple juice row; it binds the apple-containing row instead, which is where the government wrote it. Adopting 20 ug/kg here rather than 10 is not a convenience choice: it is the refusal to extend an apple-specific instrument to commodities its issuing agency did not assess.

tHg.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-mercury maximum level for a fruit juice. The sovereign mercury values in this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 total mercury at 2 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water, written for inorganic mercury at 6 ug/kg) and the fish and seafood methylmercury and total-mercury ceilings, none of which governs this product form. Mercury has no identified enrichment pathway in this supply chain, but the analyte is on the mandatory eight-total panel, so testing is mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
tHg.reference_method: Total mercury by ICP-MS (or dedicated amalgamation AAS) on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A detection above 5 ug/kg escalates to an ingredient and process-water investigation and reflexes methylmercury speciation.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a fruit juice: there is no marine bioaccumulation step in the supply chain and no anaerobic, sulfate-reducing methylation environment in the product or its process. Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) and is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury cell; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg). Methylmercury speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS or GC-ICP-MS) is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine lot test for this form.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish, seafood and other marine matrices (EU 2023/915 section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, Hong Kong Cap 132V fish entries). Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), which this row controls directly.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a methylmercury limit for this product form.

Ni.basis: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink liquid
Ni.label: EU 2024/1987 sets nickel in fruit and vegetable juices and nectars generally at 250 ug/kg and in juices and nectars from passion fruit, cocoa fruit, small fruits and berries, and coconut water at 1000 ug/kg. Both cells are named; the general cell at 250 ug/kg is the strictest applicable and binds the row.
Ni.substantiation: Direct sovereign maximum level for this exact product form, applying from 1 July 2025. Both government-written formulation bands are disclosed. As with lead, the single row ceiling is the strictest applicable across the forms in scope, so a berry or passion-fruit juice is held to 250 ug/kg rather than to its own 1000 ug/kg band; that over-compliance is stated rather than hidden. Nickel is a Tier-2 analyte.

Sn.basis: product as placed on market, ready-to-drink liquid (inorganic tin)
Sn.label: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.5.2 sets inorganic tin in canned beverages, including canned fruit and vegetable juices, at 100 mg/kg = 100000 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V sets canned beverages at 150000 ug/kg. The EU value is the strictest applicable and binds. This is a direct sovereign maximum level on the beverage-in-a-can form, not a read-across.
Sn.substantiation: Tin in a beverage is a tinplate and can-lining migration pathway, so the government instruments are written on the canned form and the canned form is where the hazard sits. The EU cell (100000 ug/kg) directly governs every canned or tinplate-packaged product in this row and is adopted as the row ceiling for all packaging formats; a carton, PET, glass or pouch format has no tin source and complies trivially, so no separate non-canned cell is published. The looser Hong Kong canned-beverage cell (150000) and the canned-foods cells for solid foods (EU 200000; Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong 250000) are disclosed and deliberately not adopted: EU writes a stricter cell specifically for beverages and HMTc preserves that product-form split. Tin is a Tier-2 analyte; an elevated result in a non-canned format is a packaging-integrity signal.

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for a fruit juice. The only sovereign aluminium values in a dietary basis are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 secondary allowable level 200 ug/kg, EU 2020/2184, Health Canada 2900 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the FSANZ infant-formula aluminium limits, which are Category 1 and are excluded from this category's anchor set by the taxonomy boundary rule. In this form aluminium is a packaging and processing signal (aluminium cans and can linings, closures, filter aids, additive carry-over) rather than a raw-material contaminant.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A result that departs materially from the applicant's own documented process baseline escalates to a packaging, can-lining and processing-aid investigation. This is a process-control tripwire, not a numeric standard: no ceiling is published because no credible sovereign maximum exists for this cell.

Cr.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for a fruit juice. The only sovereign chromium values reachable from this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 at 100 ug/kg, Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water at 50 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the public-water-system maximum contaminant levels (US EPA, Health Canada), which are water-utility instruments and not food law at all. Total chromium in this form is dominated by benign Cr(III) and is reported as a stainless-steel equipment and process-water leaching screen, not as a health limit; the health-relevant species is addressed in the Cr-VI cell.
Cr.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. An elevated result triggers the Cr(VI) speciation reflex and an equipment, process-water and ingredient investigation.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is not stable in a single-strength fruit juice. At the pH of this product form (typically pH 3.0 to 4.0, with citric, malic and ascorbic acid present) Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) by the organic acids, sugars, ascorbate and polyphenols present in the matrix, so a positive Cr(VI) result is an artifact of the total-chromium determination rather than a species present in the beverage as consumed. The reference-method basis for this determination is the in-house species arbitration at data/workbench/standards/2026-07-31-chromium-formula-adjudication.md, which found that the superseded ion-exchange plus electrothermal-AAS methods that generated the historical Cr(VI) values in liquid food matrices are not reproduced by the modern reference method: saraiva2021 (species-specific isotope dilution HPLC-ICP-MS, limit of quantification 0.049 ug/kg) quantified no Cr(VI) in any milk or formula sample while resolving Cr(III) and total chromium at single-digit ug/kg. That adjudication was drawn on a near-neutral aqueous food matrix; the acidic beverage matrices in this row are a more strongly reducing environment still, so the artifact conclusion carries a fortiori. The health-relevant species is controlled through the total-chromium cell and the reflex rule below, and this determination is a method finding, not an occurrence-derived value: no number is taken from it.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium is not a routine lot test. Total chromium (Cr cell) bounds any hexavalent fraction; a Cr(VI)-specific method (IC-ICP-MS, EN 15192 adapted to the liquid matrix) is reflexed where the total-chromium screen is elevated AND the finished-product pH is above 5.0, and a confirmed detection blocks certification pending a process and equipment investigation.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any food or beverage; every sovereign chromium value in a dietary or packaged-water basis is written for total chromium (US 21 CFR 165.110 chromium 100 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water 50 ug/kg). Cr(VI) is a species of and bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr).
Cr-VI.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for a food or beverage.
